Why planar helps here

The transformer’s primary and secondary windings are etched with the PCB, with repeatable turn placement and no bobbin or hand-wound coil. Parallel secondary layers share copper loss while the ferrite slips through routed board openings.

The GaN half bridge occupies 5.5 × 4.5 mm. Its small power stage sits beside the winding terminals, leaving the bottom free of electronic components.

The tradeoff is a more expensive eight-layer, 2 oz, filled-via board. Copper loss, proximity effects, interwinding capacitance and cooling still matter. This layout demonstrates integration; it does not establish a measured density or efficiency advantage over a conventional transformer.

Built for mounting, cabling and measurement

Four M3 holes reuse the flyback example’s actual exposed-substrate edge footprint, including its 10 mm copper exclusions. Their 71 × 49 mm pattern suits this shorter rectangular board; it differs from the flyback’s 35 × 85 mm pattern.

Polarized XT30 ports face opposite board edges. Both use pin 2 for positive and pin 1 for return. The assembly has 73 top SMT components and two top-mounted through-hole connectors. Six bare ENIG pads provide three rail/return probe pairs.

C15 now sits 5.8 mm from Q1, versus 21.74 mm previously. Primary and secondary return copper extend into the port margins. These are physical improvements for review; efficiency and loop inductance remain unmeasured.

Look inside the transformer

4:2:2 turns. Two primary layers in series; each center-tapped secondary half has two parallel copies. The center tap leaves through a layer with no winding turns.

Requested copper: 70 μm on every layer. Nominal PCB: 1.6 mm. Proposed dielectric gaps, top to bottom: 0.13 / 0.13 / 0.17 / 0.18 / 0.17 / 0.13 / 0.13 mm. The factory must confirm the delivered stack.

Two stock 0.05 mm gapped ELP22 N87 core halves give a nominal total 0.10 mm gap. The 13.12 μH magnetizing-inductance estimate uses an approximate AL of 820 nH/turn², not a measured assembled value.

The Planar Studio JSON is the four-section seed. The final six winding layers are in the native board, artwork JSON and standalone winding PCB. Regeneration instructions are in START-HERE.txt.

Power stage and calculated operating window

LMG2100R044 half bridge → 3.3 μH discrete resonant inductor → planar transformer → CSD18543Q3A synchronous rectifiers. UCC25600 controls frequency; UCC24624 controls the secondary switches. LM5164 supplies 12 V bias and TPS7A2450 supplies 5 V for GaN logic. Optocouplers provide voltage feedback and a separate output-overvoltage shutdown path.

The first prototype is scoped to a regulated 46–50 V input. The tank assumes 3.4 μH total series inductance, including 0.1 μH estimated leakage, and 200 nF C0G resonance capacitance. The controller minimum is approximately 119 kHz.

InputCalculated full-load frequencyCalculated input-impedance angle
46 V161.3 kHz+17.2°
48 V176.0 kHz+21.2°
50 V191.6 kHz+24.6°

First-harmonic screening with ideal rectification and a lumped 0.35 Ω loss assumption. All 27 selected Lr/Cr/Lm corners have an inductive full-load solution at 46 V; this is not a switching or startup simulation and does not prove ZVS. Assumed-current DC winding loss is approximately 2.85 W at 80°C; AC copper, core and other circuit losses are additional.

Unresolved: no-load/burst behavior, loop compensation, dynamic current-limit thresholds, startup overshoot, core/rectifier waveforms and thermal limits. The 12.05 V feedback and 13.27 V shutdown settings are nominal resistor calculations. No efficiency or continuous-power result has been measured.

All parts, quantities, prices and datasheet links · Catalog evidence · Core and clips list

Turnkey status: the electronics are selected from JLCPCB’s catalog, and its live quote form accepts the requested layer count, copper weight and thickness. Exact stack, filled-via processing, assembly orientation and through-hole connector soldering still need file review. JLCPCB fitting the DigiKey ferrite halves and clips is not confirmed. A fully assembled converter requires that mechanical operation to be agreed with the assembler, or completed after SMT assembly.
Required before hardware release
  1. Obtain file-level DFM acceptance for 8 layers, all-layer 2 oz, filled/capped vias, actual dielectrics, coil spacing and the three routed core openings. Verify every JLCPCB component placement against the native pad numbers.
  2. Fit the two specified gapped core halves and clips after reflow. Measure primary open-circuit inductance, short-circuit leakage, winding resistance, ratio and polarity. Tune L1/Cr to the actual transformer; do not substitute a different gap silently.
  3. Review switching behavior and compensation before power-up. On a current-limited isolated bench supply, verify 12 V bias, 5 V logic, dead time and GaN gate commands before increasing load. Measure switching-node overshoot, synchronous-rectifier timing and loss of ZVS.
  4. Validate startup, minimum load, no load, regulation, feedback failure, output overvoltage and controlled current-limit behavior. No-load regulation is specifically unproven because the controller’s nominal frequency limit overlaps its burst threshold tolerance.
  5. Ramp to 5 A only after waveforms are acceptable. Measure winding/core, GaN, MOSFET, inductor, connector and capacitor temperatures; account for ceramic-capacitor DC-bias derating. Check both output connector contacts and assess thermal rise at winding interlayer connections.

Functional isolation only. No mains, safety-barrier, surge, reverse-polarity, hot-swap or certification claim is made. Prototype manufacturing exports are included for engineering review; they are not a production-release recommendation.
